_meta.indication: SCENESSE is indicated to increase pain free light exposure in adult patients with a history of phototoxic reactions from erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, parallel group, placebo (vehicle)-controlled, double-blind study conducted in the US; subjects randomized 1:1 and received 3 implants every 2 months.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 years and older with characteristic symptoms of EPP phototoxicity and biochemically-confirmed diagnosis of EPP.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Total number of hours spent in direct sunlight between 10:00 and 18:00 hours on days when no pain was experienced (Likert score of 0).
pivotal_trials.n: 94 randomized (48 afamelanotide, 46 placebo); one placebo subject was not dispensed medication, leaving 93 dispensed/analyzed (Afa: 48, Veh: 45).
pivotal_trials.result: Median hours of pain-free direct sun exposure 69.4 (afamelanotide) vs 40.8 (placebo); Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the treatment effect 24.0 hours (95% CI 0.3, 50.3); p=0.044 (Kruskal-Wallis).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>2%): implant site reaction (21% vs 10% vehicle), nausea (19% vs 14%), oropharyngeal pain, cough, fatigue, skin hyperpigmentation, dizziness, melanocytic nevus. No deaths; serious adverse events occurred in 4% of subjects.
target_moa: Afamelanotide is an alpha-melanocyte stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH) analogue that acts as a melanocortin-1 receptor (MC1R) agonist, stimulating melanogenesis (eumelanin), which provides photoprotection by absorbing and scattering light.
modality: Peptide (13-amino acid synthetic peptide analogue of alpha-MSH), a new molecular entity.

rems.type: A REMS is not needed; professional labeling, routine pharmacovigilance, and postmarketing studies are adequate to manage the risk.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was held for this NDA because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues in the intended population.

orphan_indication.text: Granted orphan drug designation on July 17, 2008 for [Nle4, D-Phe7]-alpha-melanocyte stimulating hormone for treatment of erythropoietic porphyria (Designation #08-2632).

basis.text: The application was granted priority review status (notified January 7, 2019).

summary.text: SCENESSE was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA for a new molecular entity for EPP; it received orphan drug designation (2008), Fast Track designation (2016), and priority review, and was approved first cycle without an advisory committee. It was not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: Clinuvel, Inc. submitted a New Drug Application (NDA) 210797 for Scenesse (afamelanotide) implant, 16 mg [REDACTED] (b) (4) in erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) under the 505(b)(1) regulatory pathway.

The Applicant submitted a request for orphan drug designation on May 16, 2008, and on July 17, 2008 was granted orphan drug designation for [Nle4, D-Phe7]-\alpha-melanocyte stimulating hormone for “treatment of erythropoietic porphyria” (Designation #08-2632).
On April 28, 2016, the Applicant submitted a request for Fast Track designation to the IND and received Fast Track designation on June 29, 2016.
The Applicant was notified of priority review status and acceptance of NDA filing on January 7, 2019 and January 9, 2019 respectively.

requirement.text: Conduct a thorough QT clinical study to adequately characterize the effect of afamelanotide on cardiac repolarization.

requirement.text: Conduct a prospective, longitudinal, registry-based observational exposure cohort study to collect long-term safety data on afamelanotide in EPP patients in the US, with patients followed for a minimum of eight years from treatment initiation.

citations.quote: 3726-2 Conduct a prospective, longitudinal, registry based observational exposure cohort study to collect information on long-term safety of afamelanotide in patients with erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) in the United States. Patients will be followed for a minimum of eight years from initiation of treatment with afamelanotide.
